What is the TAC Pipeline?

The TAC (Taxonomy-Agnostic Clustering) pipeline takes the clean, denoised ZOTUs (Amplicon Sequence Variants) and clusters them at 98.7% sequence similarity — the standard threshold for bacterial species — without using any prior taxonomy labels.

This approach gives you the best of both worlds: it eliminates sequencing noise and PCR errors via denoising first, and then groups closely related variants into biologically sensible, species-level operational units.

Below is an explanation of each output file in this folder and how to use it.

1Primary Abundance Tables

Table
OTUs-Table-TAC.tab
What it is
A tab-separated text table containing the abundance count of each TAC OTU cluster in each sample. Rows are TAC OTUs (clustered at 98.7% similarity), columns are your sample IDs, and the last column shows the assigned taxonomy (Domain down to Species).
Use it for
This is the primary abundance table for TAC mode. Open it in Microsoft Excel, R, Python, or statistical software to analyze microbiome diversity and compare microbial communities between sample groups.
Table
SampleMinCount_Normalized-OTUs-Table-TAC.tab
What it is
A depth-normalized version of the TAC abundance table where all samples are subsampled (rarefied) to match the sequencing depth of the sample with the fewest reads.
Use it for
Unbiased statistical comparisons of alpha and beta diversity across samples with different library sizes.
Table
Spike_Normalized-OTUs-Table-TAC.tabPresent only if spike-ins were used
What it is
An abundance table normalized against internal DNA spike-in standards added to your samples before sequencing.
Use it for
Estimating absolute microbial abundance (cell or copy numbers per unit of sample) instead of relative percentages.

2Sequence Files and Traceability Mappings

Sequences
OTUs-Seqs-TAC.fasta
What it is
A FASTA file containing the representative (centroid) DNA sequence for each TAC OTU cluster, with taxonomy in the headers.
Use it for
Sequence searches (BLAST), alignments, and phylogenetic analyses of the clustered representative sequences.
Mapping
Map-ZOTUs-OTUs-TAC.tab
What it is
A two-column mapping table that connects each original ZOTU identifier to the TAC OTU cluster it was assigned to.
Use it for
Full traceability. Use this file if you need to know which exact sequence variants (ZOTUs) were merged into a given TAC OTU.

3Phylogenetic Trees

Tree
OTUs-Tree-nj-TAC.tre
What it is
A phylogenetic tree of the TAC OTU centroid sequences in standard Newick format (.tre), built using Neighbor-Joining.
Use it for
Tree-based diversity analyses (such as UniFrac) in QIIME 2 or phyloseq, and visualization in tree viewers like FigTree or iTOL.

4Interactive Visualizations

Interactive
OTUs-Krona.html
What it is
An interactive Krona plot chart of taxonomic proportions.
Use it for
Double-click to open in any web browser and explore the taxonomic breakdown of your TAC OTUs visually.

5SILVA 144+ Dual Outputs (*-8Levels.*)

Generated when a reference database with bacterial kingdoms is used, e.g. SILVA >= 144

Table
OTUs-Table-TAC-8Levels.tab
OTUs-Seqs-TAC-8Levels.fasta
OTUs-Krona-8Levels.html
SampleMinCount_Normalized-OTUs-Table-TAC-8Levels.tab
Spike_Normalized-OTUs-Table-TAC-8Levels.tabIf spike-ins were used
What they are
The exact same TAC results as above, but with 8 taxonomic ranks including the bacterial Kingdom rank (e.g., Bacillati, Pseudomonadati).
Use them for
Use the *-8Levels files for the latest SILVA 144+ taxonomy, or use the standard files for downstream tools expecting 7 levels.
